findings.highlight: at her full potential
findings.evidenceJa: 一人前
findings.governingReading: Rin is fully qualified or accomplished as both magus and Master.
findings.explanation: Full potential claims she has reached her maximum possible power rather than ordinary full competence.

findings.highlight: a Master now
findings.evidenceJa: 歴としたマスター
findings.governingReading: Rin calls Shirou a proper, indisputable Master.
findings.explanation: The English gives only current status and omits her emphatic validation.

findings.highlight: …Like the girl Illya, leaves a cold warning.
findings.evidenceJa: あのイリヤという少女と同じように、冷たい警告を残していった。
findings.governingReading: Like Illya, the departing possible ally leaves him a cold warning.
findings.explanation: The English is a subjectless fragment and awkwardly attaches the comparison.

findings.highlight: the incident last nightwhen I saw
findings.evidenceJa: 昨夜の事件夜の学校で
findings.governingReading: The phrase appositionally specifies last night’s incident at the school.
findings.explanation: Missing spacing fuses “night” and “when” at a key chronology recap.

findings.highlight: I can’t do that.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にはそんな芸当はさせられない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes he cannot make Saber perform the feat of entering spirit form.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the agent and object unspecified, sounding as though Shirou himself cannot become a spirit.

findings.highlight: Sitting in a Japanese-style
findings.evidenceJa: 正座したセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber sits formally in seiza on the wooden floor.
findings.explanation: The English is ungrammatical and replaces the named posture with vague cultural shorthand.

findings.highlight: SoI should not follow a wrong path with her.
findings.evidenceJa: ならこの先、自分が間違った道を進む事はないだろう。
findings.governingReading: Shirou reasons that with such a sacred-seeming companion he will not proceed down a mistaken path.
findings.explanation: The missing space visibly fuses the inference and pronoun.

findings.highlight: is surprisingly suited to this place.
findings.evidenceJa: ひどくこの道場にあっていた。
findings.governingReading: Her permeating voice suits the dojo extremely well.
findings.explanation: Surprisingly invents Shirou’s violated expectation and removes the degree of harmony.

findings.highlight: make me conscious of her womanhood
findings.evidenceJa: 異性を意識してしまう
findings.governingReading: Her realistic clothes force Shirou to become conscious of her as a member of the opposite sex.
findings.explanation: Womanhood is more abstract and sexualized, changing his awkward relational awareness.

findings.highlight: I’m troubled
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女は苦手だが
findings.governingReading: He finds Saber difficult to deal with or feels awkward around her.
findings.explanation: The English loses Saber as the source and turns relational discomfort into unspecified trouble.

findings.highlight: Whadon’t be stupid.
findings.evidenceJa: なバカ言ってんな
findings.governingReading: Shirou bursts out, “D-Don’t be stupid.”
findings.explanation: The English fuses a false start with the next phrase into the nonword “Whadon’t.”

findings.highlight: I’ll thank you for that.
findings.evidenceJa: それに関しては礼を言う
findings.governingReading: Shirou gives thanks here and now for being carried home.
findings.explanation: The future construction sounds like a promise to thank her later and redundantly follows “I’m grateful.”

findings.highlight: There’s no room for me to question her about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の意思には疑問を挟む余地などない。
findings.governingReading: The certainty and firmness of Saber’s intention leave no room for doubt.
findings.explanation: The English turns an observation about her resolve into a conversational restriction on Shirou asking questions.

findings.highlight: beings that have reached the rank of gods
findings.evidenceJa: 神域まで上り詰めた存在
findings.governingReading: Through individual power they rose into a divine or godlike domain.
findings.explanation: Rank of gods promotes figurative or categorical proximity to literal god status.

findings.highlight: supernatural abilities
findings.evidenceJa: 卓越した能力
findings.governingReading: The heroes possessed outstanding abilities in life.
findings.explanation: Supernatural adds an ontological claim absent from “exceptional.”

findings.highlight: Those are the seven classes.
findings.evidenceJa: この世界に我々が存在できる依り代を用意したのです。
findings.governingReading: The Grail prepared vessels or anchors that permit the summoned Heroic Spirits to exist in this world.
findings.explanation: The English omits the anchoring function entirely and jumps directly from compatible vessels to class labels.

findings.highlight: those who receive these classes are called Servants.
findings.evidenceJa: 役割という殻を被ったモノが、サーヴァントと呼ばれる
findings.governingReading: A Heroic Spirit clothed in the shell of a role is called a Servant.
findings.explanation: Receiving a class removes the shell/vessel mechanism and its relation to bounded manifestation.

findings.highlight: that is also the weakness of the Saber class.
findings.evidenceJa: それがセイバーの欠点でもある。
findings.governingReading: Saber says that this is also her own drawback.
findings.explanation: The English turns a first-person limitation into a universal rule about the entire class.

findings.highlight: stronger than you in combat
findings.evidenceJa: 自身より白兵戦で優れている場合
findings.governingReading: If an enemy surpasses you specifically in close combat.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the hypothetical from melee superiority to overall combat superiority, weakening the logic for changing methods.

findings.highlight: I’d have to do something without fightin
findings.evidenceJa: 戦わずになんとかするしかな
findings.governingReading: Shirou begins to say he would have to manage without fighting directly.
findings.explanation: The English is visibly truncated mid-word.

findings.highlight: beat them some other way.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣以外で敵の息の根を絶つ
findings.governingReading: If the sword cannot prevail, the opponent may end the enemy’s life by another means.
findings.explanation: “Beat” euphemizes the lethal alternative that shocks Shirou into understanding indirect tactics.

findings.highlight: Servants that lack ability
findings.evidenceJa: 能力に劣ったサーヴァント
findings.governingReading: Servants whose capabilities are inferior in the relevant confrontation will exhaust every method.
findings.explanation: Lack ability turns relative disadvantage into general incompetence.

findings.highlight:
an
a special
ability to hide its presence
findings.evidenceJa: 気配を隠すという能力
findings.governingReading: Assassin has the ability to conceal its presence despite low parameters.
findings.explanation: mirror moon prints three competing article/adjective variants, breaking the sentence.

findings.highlight: have our guaranteed fatal attack.
findings.evidenceJa: 必殺の機会を持っている
findings.governingReading: Every Heroic Spirit possesses an opportunity or means to deliver a decisive killing blow.
findings.explanation: A guaranteed fatal attack converts potential and opportunity into certainty of outcome.

findings.highlight: That is the ‘Noble Phantasm’the trump card
findings.evidenceJa: それが“宝具”サーヴァントたちの切り札
findings.governingReading: The Noble Phantasm is the Servants’ trump card.
findings.explanation: Missing punctuation/spacing fuses the term and its appositive.

findings.highlight: a strange amount of magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: 桁違いの魔力
findings.governingReading: Shirou felt magical energy of an entirely different order in Lancer’s utterance.
findings.explanation: Strange changes overwhelming magnitude into oddness.

findings.highlight: recitement of the true name
findings.evidenceJa: 詠唱真名による覚醒
findings.governingReading: A Noble Phantasm awakens through the incantatory utterance of its true name.
findings.explanation: “Recitement” is not standard English and obscures the written/ruby relation between incantation and true name.

findings.highlight: In exchange for revealing the name
findings.evidenceJa: 正体を明かすかわりに
findings.governingReading: In exchange for revealing the Servant’s identity, the Noble Phantasm releases its decisive blow.
findings.explanation: Name narrows the cost; the preceding explanation is that the weapon name exposes identity and weakness.

findings.highlight: expose all its weaknesses.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの欠点をもさらけ出す
findings.governingReading: Failure also exposes the Servant’s vulnerability or flaw.
findings.explanation: The English adds “all,” claiming comprehensive disclosure.

findings.highlight: Uhum, can you really
findings.evidenceJa: ぁその、本当に
findings.governingReading: Saber begins with a hesitant “Ah, um.”
findings.explanation: The English fuses the hesitation into the assent-like form “Uhum.”

findings.highlight: Servants themselves are powerful magics.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントはそれ自体が強力な魔力ですから。
findings.governingReading: A Servant is itself a powerful concentration or source of magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English changes magical energy into plural acts or systems of magic.

findings.highlight: Ughthat could be true.
findings.evidenceJa: うそれはそうだけどな。
findings.governingReading: Shirou concedes hesitantly that this is so.
findings.explanation: The English fuses interjection and clause and weakens the concession to mere possibility.

findings.highlight: its only natural
findings.evidenceJa: 当然です
findings.governingReading: Saber says it is natural that their contract lets him grasp her condition.
findings.explanation: The contraction lacks its apostrophe in a formal explanatory line.

findings.highlight: some classify according to animals.
findings.evidenceJa: 獣に喩えて見分けるマスター
findings.governingReading: Some Masters distinguish abilities by comparing them to beasts.
findings.explanation: Animal classification sounds like taxonomy and removes the figurative personal visualization.

findings.highlight: the calm eyes of a swordsman
findings.evidenceJa: 冷徹な剣士の目
findings.governingReading: Her eyes are those of a cold, uncompromising swordsman who permits no denial.
findings.explanation: Calm removes severity and emotional coldness from Saber’s pressure.

findings.highlight: I stare back, trying not to lose
findings.evidenceJa: それに気圧されまいと視線を返して
findings.governingReading: Shirou returns her gaze so as not to be overawed by it.
findings.explanation: Trying not to lose recasts resistance to intimidation as a contest.

findings.highlight: I can’t survive this without doing anything.
findings.evidenceJa: 無傷で、何もしないままじゃ生き残れない
findings.governingReading: He knows he cannot survive both unhurt and inactive.
findings.explanation: The English omits “unscathed,” narrowing his recognition of unavoidable cost.

findings.highlight: I don’t feel anything toward the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯なんて言われても実感が湧かない。
findings.governingReading: Talk of the Grail still has no felt reality for Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English turns lack of experiential reality into absence of emotion toward the object.

findings.highlight: not to involve any unnecessary people.
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人を巻き込まないように
findings.governingReading: He will do everything possible not to involve unrelated bystanders.
findings.explanation: Calling people unnecessary evaluates their usefulness rather than their lack of involvement.

findings.highlight: a second-hand ideal from my father
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣の受け売り
findings.governingReading: Shirou explicitly identifies the principle as borrowed from Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: Father removes the named callback and substitutes a relational title.
